1.  Save a copy with your surname (for example, `ADE3_diversity_Smith.Rmd`) in the same folder as `ADE3_class_data_frozen.csv`.
2.  Work through the sections in order, alongside the handout. Run a whole chunk by clicking its green arrow, or run a single line with Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on a Mac). Read the output before moving on.

## 3.1 What Shannon and Simpson measure

Calculate $H'$ and $1 - D$ by hand for each community first, then check your answers.

-   Community A: three species with counts 5, 3 and 2.
-   Community B: four species with counts 7, 1, 1 and 1.

```{r mini-problem}
diversity(c(5, 3, 2))                         # Shannon H', community A
diversity(c(7, 1, 1, 1))                      # Shannon H', community B
diversity(c(5, 3, 2), index = "simpson")      # Gini-Simpson (1 - D), community A
diversity(c(7, 1, 1, 1), index = "simpson")   # Gini-Simpson (1 - D), community B
```

Which community has more species? Which is more diverse? Why do these differ?

## 3.2 Load and clean the class data

A "New names" message is expected when the file is read, because two columns have no header.

```{r load-data}
arth <- read_csv("ADE3_class_data_frozen.csv",
                 col_types = cols(.default = "c"),   # read every column as text
                 na = c("", "NA", "-", "n/a")) %>%   # treat blanks and placeholders as missing
  rename(Surname = 1) %>%                            # name the unheaded first column
  select(-starts_with("...")) %>%                    # drop the empty unnamed column
  filter(!is.na(Initials))                           # drop blank rows

nrow(arth)    # number of specimen records
names(arth)   # check the column names
```

Standardise the names, then apply the corrections table.

```{r clean-data}
# Standardise capitalisation and remove stray spaces
arth <- arth %>%
  mutate(across(matches("^(Class|Order|Family|Genus)_"), ~ str_to_title(str_squish(.x))),
         Habitat = str_to_title(str_squish(Habitat)))

# Corrections: each entry reads "as typed" = "corrected". Add any new ones you find.
fixes <- c(
  # Class
  "Insects" = "Insecta", "Insect" = "Insecta",
  "Pancrustacea" = "Insecta",                # Pancrustacea is above class level
  "Malacosraca" = "Malacostraca",
  # Order
  "Harvestmen" = "Opiliones", "Opilones" = "Opiliones", "Opilinoes" = "Opiliones",
  "Neuropotera" = "Neuroptera", "Diptera (True Flies)" = "Diptera",
  # Family
  "Phalangiid" = "Phalangiidae", "Phalangiid Harvestman" = "Phalangiidae",
  "Syphridae" = "Syrphidae", "Scathophlagidae" = "Scathophagidae",
  "Aculeta" = "Vespidae",                    # Aculeata is an infraorder, typed in the Family column
  "Sclerosomatidae/Phalangiidae" = "Sclerosomatidae",   # Leiobunum is a sclerosomatid
  # Genus
  "Procellio" = "Porcellio", "Episyrphyus" = "Episyrphus",
  # Habitat
  "Outside Ashworth" = "Ashworth Trees",     # same coordinates as an Ashworth Trees record
  "Ashworth Medows" = "Ashworth Meadows",
  "Nucleus" = "Nucleus Mound", "Nucleus Mounds" = "Nucleus Mound",
  "Murchison House" = "Murchison"
)

# Replace any name found in the corrections table; keep all other names as they are
arth <- arth %>%
  mutate(across(c(matches("^(Class|Order|Family|Genus)_"), Habitat),
                ~ coalesce(unname(fixes[.x]), .x)))
```

Check what is left. Look for typos, near-duplicates and names at the wrong rank.

```{r check-data}
count(arth, Habitat, sort = TRUE)
count(arth, Family_Morphology, sort = TRUE)
count(arth, Family_AI, sort = TRUE)
count(arth, Family_DNA, sort = TRUE)
```

Did you find any names that still need correcting? If so, add them to `fixes` and rerun the clean-data chunk.

## 3.3 Choose your taxonomic level and identification source

```{r best-id}
# Best available ID at each rank: DNA first, then morphology, then AI
arth <- arth %>%
  mutate(Class_Best  = coalesce(Class_DNA,  Class_Morphology,  Class_AI),
         Order_Best  = coalesce(Order_DNA,  Order_Morphology,  Order_AI),
         Family_Best = coalesce(Family_DNA, Family_Morphology, Family_AI),
         Genus_Best  = coalesce(Genus_DNA,  Genus_Morphology,  Genus_AI))
```

Set the two choices that the rest of the analysis depends on.

```{r choose-level}
level     <- "Family"   # "Class", "Order", "Family" or "Genus"
id_source <- "Best"     # "Best", "DNA", "Morphology" or "AI"

arth_lvl <- arth %>%
  mutate(taxon = .data[[paste(level, id_source, sep = "_")]]) %>%
  filter(!is.na(taxon), !is.na(Habitat))

nrow(arth)       # all specimen records
nrow(arth_lvl)   # records identified at your chosen level
```

How many specimens did you lose by choosing this level?

Answer:

Compare the identification sources at your chosen level.

```{r compare-sources}
sources <- c("AI", "Morphology", "DNA", "Best")

data.frame(
  source     = sources,
  identified = sapply(sources, function(s) sum(!is.na(arth[[paste(level, s, sep = "_")]]))),
  taxa       = sapply(sources, function(s) n_distinct(arth[[paste(level, s, sep = "_")]], na.rm = TRUE))
)
```

## 3.4 Diversity by habitat

```{r diversity-by-habitat}
# Community matrix: one row per habitat, one column per taxon, cells are counts
comm <- arth_lvl %>%
  count(Habitat, taxon) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = taxon, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("Habitat")

N <- rowSums(comm)                       # specimens per habitat
S <- specnumber(comm)                    # richness
H <- diversity(comm, index = "shannon")  # Shannon's H'
J <- H / log(S)                          # Pielou's evenness (NaN if S = 1)
G <- diversity(comm, index = "simpson")  # Gini-Simpson, 1 - D

div_table <- data.frame(N, S, H = round(H, 2), J = round(J, 2), Simpson = round(G, 2))
div_table
```

Which habitat has the highest richness? Which has the highest $H'$? If the answers differ, use $J'$ to explain why.

Answer:

## 3.5 Sampling effort and rarefaction

```{r rarefaction}
N   # check specimens per habitat first

# Habitats with very few specimens drag every habitat down to a tiny sample size.
# If needed, drop them before rarefying by removing the # from the next two lines:
# comm <- comm[N >= 5, ]
# N <- rowSums(comm)

rarefy(comm, sample = min(N))            # expected taxa at equal sample size
rarecurve(comm, step = 1, label = TRUE)  # rarefaction curve for each habitat
```

Does the ranking of habitats change after rarefaction? If so, what does that tell you about the raw comparison in section 3.4?

## 3.6 Collector's curve

```{r specimen-matrix}
# Matrix with one row per specimen
spec_mat <- arth_lvl %>%
  mutate(specimen = row_number(), present = 1) %>%
  select(specimen, taxon, present) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = taxon, values_from = present, values_fill = 0) %>%
  select(-specimen)
```

```{r collectors-curve}
# Two curves: the order in the sheet, and the average of 100 random orders
set.seed(1)
curve_order  <- specaccum(spec_mat, method = "collector")
curve_random <- specaccum(spec_mat, method = "random", permutations = 100)

# Extract the numbers from each curve into a data frame for ggplot
random_df <- tibble(specimens = curve_random$sites,
                    taxa      = curve_random$richness,
                    sd        = curve_random$sd)

order_df  <- tibble(specimens = curve_order$sites,
                    taxa      = curve_order$richness)

# Build the plot and store it, so it can be saved in section 3.7
curve_plot <- ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = random_df,
              aes(x = specimens, ymin = taxa - 2 * sd, ymax = taxa + 2 * sd),
              fill = "lightblue") +
  geom_line(data = random_df,
            aes(x = specimens, y = taxa, colour = "random"),
            linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(data = order_df,
            aes(x = specimens, y = taxa, colour = "sheet"),
            linewidth = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(random = "blue", sheet = "red"),
                      labels = c(random = "Random order (mean \u00B1 2 SD)",   # \u00B1 is the ± sign
                                 sheet  = "Sheet order")) +
  labs(x = "Specimens identified",
       y = paste0("Cumulative number of taxa (", level, ")"),
       colour = NULL) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

curve_plot

# Estimate total richness from rare taxa (singletons and doubletons)
estimateR(colSums(spec_mat))
```

Does the red curve differ from the blue curve? Why does randomising the order give a fairer curve?

Answer:

## 3.7.1 Save your outputs

The file names record your chosen level and source, so outputs from different runs do not overwrite each other.

```{r save-outputs}
# Diversity table
write_csv(rownames_to_column(div_table, "Habitat"),
          paste0("diversity_table_", level, "_", id_source, ".csv"))

# Collector's curve
ggsave(paste0("collectors_curve_", level, "_", id_source, ".png"),
       plot = curve_plot, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 200)

# Rarefaction curves (still drawn with base graphics)
png(paste0("rarefaction_", level, "_", id_source, ".png"),
    width = 1600, height = 1200, res = 200)
rarecurve(comm, step = 1, label = TRUE)
dev.off()
```
